To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the broadband impedance model is useful in predicting microwave instability, that the microwave instability threshold is a factor of 4 lower than the nominal operating current in KEKB, that the combined effects of beam-beam and microwave instability are important in the study of beam-beam effects, and that the asymmetry in the beam-beam effect can be explained by a combination of beam-beam effect and microwave instability.
the broadband wakefields and their effect on the beam-beam interactions have been studied and understood.

we have successfully modeled the microwave instability in KEKB using a broadband impedance approach, which is a first for a storage ring, and we have demonstrated the effects of the microwave instability on the beam-beam dynamics in a realistic storage ring environment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of potential well distortion, microwave instability, and their combined effects on beam-beam interactions in colliding beam storage rings.
the longitudinal wakefield and its effects with colliding beams at KEKB.
the potential-well distortion, microwave instability, and the combined effect with beam-beam interactions in the low energy KEKB.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the potential well distortion and the microwave instability are the two major factors that limit the luminosity of KEKB.
the potential-well distortion is the dominant effect for the observed emittance growth in the KEKB low energy ring.
the beam-beam effect in KEKB is a strong function of the beam current and the bunch length.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the potential well distortion due to microwave instability is a significant factor in the beam-beam interaction and it should be taken into account in future beam-beam studies.
we have developed a model to predict longitudinal dynamics in KEKB.
the microwave instability in KEKB is a serious concern and the combined effects of the beam-beam and the microwave instability should be taken into account when the KEKB luminosity is increased.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the longitudinal dynamics and beam-beam interaction are closely connected, which can not be ignored when studying high intensity beam physics.

we have a good understanding of the longitudinal dynamics in KEKB, and that the combined effects of the microwave instability and the beam-beam interaction are very important for the future KEK-B factory.
the microwave instability is an essential component of the beam-beam dynamics and should not be neglected in the beam-beam simulations.
